question.problem:
$$
\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ 2 & -3 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}]}}=\overset{Q}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{q}_{11} & {q}_{12} \\ {q}_{21} & {q}_{22} \\ {q}_{31} & {q}_{32}\end{aligned}]}}\overset{R}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{r}_{11} & {r}_{12} \\ 0 & {r}_{22}\end{aligned}]}}.
$$

Consider the QR factorization of the matrix $A$ shown above. Given that the columns ${q}_{1},{q}_{2}$ of $Q$ were obtained from the columns of $A$ using the Gram-Schmidt process, find  the value of ${q}_{11}\cdot {r}_{12}.$
question.worked_solution:
Let ${a}_{1},{a}_{2}$ be the columns of $A.$

First, we find an orthonormal basis of $\text{Col}(A)=\text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\}$ using the Gram-Schmidt process.

**Step 1**. We set ${v}_{1}={a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

**Step 2**. We find the vector ${v}_{2}$ orthogonal to $\text{Span}\{{v}_{1}\}$ using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{2} & ={a}_{2}-{\text{proj}}_{{v}_{1}}{a}_{2} \\  & ={a}_{2}-\frac{{a}_{2}\cdot {v}_{1}}{{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}}{v}_{1} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -3 \\ 3\end{aligned}]-(-\frac{9}{9})[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -3 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1 \\ 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we normalize ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{q}_{1} & =\frac{{v}_{1}}{‖{v}_{1}‖}=\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ {q}_{2} & =\frac{{v}_{2}}{‖{v}_{2}‖}=\frac{1}{3\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1 \\ 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute $R:$

$$
\begin{aligned}R & ={Q}^{T}\,A \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3} & \frac{2}{3} & \frac{1}{3} \\ -\frac{1}{3\sqrt{2}} & -\frac{1}{3\sqrt{2}} & \frac{4}{3\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ 2 & -3 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -3 \\ 0 & 3\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain the following QR factorization of $A:$

$$
\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ 2 & -3 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}]}}=\overset{Q}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3} & -\frac{1}{3\sqrt{2}} \\ \frac{2}{3} & -\frac{1}{3\sqrt{2}} \\ \frac{1}{3} & \frac{4}{3\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}]}}\overset{R}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}3 & -3 \\ 0 & 3\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}]}}.
$$

Finally, ${q}_{11}\cdot {r}_{12}=(\frac{2}{3})\cdot (-3)=-2.$
